worked_solution:
Given an invertible $n\times n$ matrix $A,$ we have

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}.
$$

First, we find $|A|$ using a Laplace expansion across the $2$nd column:

$$
\begin{aligned}|A| & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 5 \\ -4 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+1(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+(-1)(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(-12+2)+(9-5)+(-6+20) \\  & =20+4+14 \\  & =38\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
|{A}^{-1}|=\frac{1}{|A|}=\frac{1}{38}.
$$
